name: Ecdysterone

lead: Ecdysterone, or 20-hydroxyecdysone, is the main molting hormone of insects and crustaceans and is also found in plants such as spinach and Cyanotis. It is sold as a supplement and is being developed as an investigational drug for some muscle conditions.

A widely cited study in young men reported greater muscle gains with high-dose ecdysterone alongside training; replication is lacking and other findings are mixed, so the evidence is considered preliminary.

paras: In rodents ecdysterone stimulates muscle protein synthesis without androgen receptor activity, with evidence pointing to estrogen receptor beta and downstream Akt signalling. Human mechanism data are limited.

Acute toxicity appears low. It is sold as a supplement, but the World Anti-Doping Agency has monitored it, and product purity is reported to be variable. Long-term human safety has not been established.
